title: Debug Flare: Interactive Payload Etching & Error Taxonomy Canvas
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design an interactive diagnostics surface for the Redwood Console that lets engineers rapidly 'etch' a failed request into layered views: raw payload, normalized payload diff, inferred error taxonomy, KV cache state at failure, and retry provenance. The goal is to reduce mean time to triage for production failures by enabling quick hypothesis iteration and safe retry decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Designer prototype demonstrates the etched-layer toggles and linked timeline scrubber; 2) PM and Eng sign-off on taxonomy mapping for top 10 error types; 3) Prototype connects to mock logs and shows retry provenance for at least two retry strategies; 4) Usability test (5 engineers) completes with task success >= 80% and median task time under 6 minutes.
decisions: Use layered 'etch' metaphor rather than modal dialogs to keep context while drilling; chosen for faster mental model during triage.
Surface inferred error taxonomy (transient, resource, model, request-validation) as first-class filters — trade-off: requires backend mapping; Eng agreed to provide mapping endpoint (ENG-60122).
Keep KV cache snapshot read-only and time-limited to protect PII; full dump requires elevated permission and audit logging.
Implement lightweight payload diffing client-side using streaming comparator to avoid heavy server CPU during preview.
Opted not to include full replay-by-default — add as opt-in to avoid accidental side-effects (safety-first).
review_comments: PM Leila Ortiz (2026-03-02): 'Love the etching metaphor; confirm that inferred taxonomy maps to existing alerting groups.'
Eng Tech Lead Omar Patel (2026-03-05): 'Concern about KV snapshot size for long requests — recommend truncation and sampling; will prototype ENG-60203.'
Security Review (2026-03-07) from Anya Singh: 'Client-side diffing + audit-gated full dump is acceptable; add explicit UI guardrail when payload contains potential secrets.'
Design Peer Feedback from Marco Liu (2026-03-08): 'Consider a compact breadcrumb so users can jump to retry origin or upstream service traces.'
next_steps: Address Eng feedback about KV snapshot truncation; pair with Omar to define API contract (week of 2026-03-15).
Add UI guardrail for payloads flagged by secrets detector; request security re-review once implemented.
Run moderated usability sessions with 6 engineers across infra and application teams and capture task timings (target complete by 2026-03-18).
Wire up taxonomy filters to alerts dashboard prototype and demonstrate correlated view during roadmap review.
Create engineering handoff doc with component specs, accessible states, and ARIA guidance.
notes: User problem: Engineers open 8+ tabs during triage (logs, traces, payload store). This design consolidates those views in a single etch canvas.
Metrics target: reduce triage time for failed requests by 25% for high-volume customers within 90 days of release.
Accessibility: ensure keyboard-first etch navigation and screen-reader labeling for each layer control.
